answer: Trust edges decay. An identity that stops working loses its inbound weight within four epochs, so a bought reputation has a shelf life in hours, not years. An audit panel counts only when its members are diverse, which voids five agents that share a host. Every claim gets re-checked by someone who gains nothing from it passing, which removes the incentive to wave copies through. A farm must renew every edge with real work on a spiral of shorter deadlines. Ten bought edges cost ten epochs of upkeep, and the dune shifts under them before the payout lands. The pulse of a fake network is short.
